market_holds: Spot is $28.44 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-24), -15.3% over 20 sessions and -19.8% from the 52-week high. The front-week straddle implies an 8.24% event move, against a median 3.62% over the last 8 prints. Downside is paid: 25-delta skew is +7.6 vol points, and put/call open interest is 0.67. Yahoo earningsTrend, read today: Q4 consensus EPS $0.741 (13 analysts, $0.71-0.79) on revenue $15.30B ($14.34-15.87B); Q1 FY27 EPS $0.711 on $14.76B; FY27 EPS $3.147 ($2.75-3.54, 18 analysts). The FY27 number was $3.138 sixty days ago and $3.153 thirty days ago, so it has not been cut since IDC (Oct 8), Intel (Oct 30), TrendForce (Nov 11) or Lenovo (Nov 19). HP's own Q4 guide is $0.69-0.79 non-GAAP, which includes $0.08 of tariff refunds, and FY26 is $3.19-3.29 including $0.19 of refunds, so underlying FY26 is about $3.05. Earnings Whispers has a $0.90 whisper. Short interest is 9.9% of float, 6.1 days to cover (Oct 30 settlement). Mean target is $27.55 and the rating is Hold. The run-in is tied to dated outside news, not to HP's own: on Oct 30 the stock fell about 9.6% (31.83 to 28.78) when Intel forecast about a 10% PC unit decline in 2027; it rose about 6% on Nov 4 when the Walmsley CEO appointment was announced; it then traded flat at 28-29 while SPY fell about 6% and Dell and Lenovo collapsed. Last four print reactions: -1.4, +0.05, -1.88, -2.92. They turned on the guide and memory-margin tone, not on EPS beats.
view: HPQ trades on the FY27 guide, which HP said on its Q3 call it would give on this call. Two outside inputs have moved against HP's August framing, and sell-side numbers have not followed. First, the industry: HP's Sept 21 8-K planning assumption was a mid-single-digit decline in calendar-2027 industry PC units. Intel has since called it at about -10% after about -12% in 2026. IDC has HP's Jul-Sep units at -30.9% against -20.1% for the industry, so HP is losing share. TrendForce still sees PC DRAM contract prices up 13-18% QoQ in Q4. Lenovo posted its first operating loss since 2017 and expects the memory shortage to last through 2027. Second, the numbers: FY27 consensus of $3.15 means about 3% growth over underlying FY26 of $3.05, even though H2 FY26 is running at about $0.66-0.72 a quarter excluding refunds. Q4 revenue consensus of $15.30B implies Personal Systems of about $11.15B, up 7% YoY, which on about -30% units needs ASP up about 53%. Q3 delivered about +40%, so revenue looks more likely to miss modestly than beat. My arithmetic puts FY27 at about $2.95-3.10 and the guide midpoint below $3.15 at about 60-65%. HP has also guided below consensus at the start of the year before (FY26). Two things stop this from being a short. The price has already absorbed much of it: the Intel-day drop, about 9x consensus FY27, a mean target below spot, paid downside skew and 10% short interest mean a modest guide shortfall is probably near the buy-side bar. And there are real upside levers: Q4 EPS has a whisper above the guide top and two prior quarters beat by 14-15 cents; DRAM spot prices have been slipping since early November, which gives management room to say input costs are peaking; and a crowded short can squeeze on any 'trough is behind us' language. Dell reports the same evening and the tape has been moving 2-5% a day, so overnight noise is large. Net: a modest lean down, not a bet.
unpriced: Possibly the FY27 sell-side number. It is stale at $3.147 and has not been revised after Intel's -10% call for 2027 units, IDC's -31% HP units, or the continued rise in DRAM contract prices, so a guide midpoint near $2.95-3.05 would look like a miss against the printed consensus. Most of this looks priced on the buy-side, though: the Oct 30 drop came with the Intel news, and positioning and skew already lean down. I cannot show the buy-side bar is above a likely guide, so the gap is real against consensus but probably not against the price.

recommendation.reason: The mechanism is a stale FY27 consensus ($3.15, unrevised over 60 days) against worse unit and memory inputs since HP last spoke, plus a probable modest Q4 revenue miss on units of about -30%. The price already moved about 10% on the Intel PC warning, sits at about 9x FY27 with 10% short interest and paid downside skew, and HP's own EPS track record and softening DRAM spot prices give real upside paths. The downside lean does not reach 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An FY27 EPS guide with a midpoint at or above about $3.10, plus an explicit statement that memory input costs have peaked, or a step-up in the buyback. With 10% short interest that would gap the stock up.

self_critique: The downside case rests on a stale sell-side number, but the stock already fell about 10% on the very news that makes it stale, short interest is high, and HP's 2026 pattern is to beat and raise from conservative guides (FY26 raised twice). A wide FY27 range around $3.00-3.20 with 'trough behind us' language, plus softer DRAM spot prices and a buyback at a 12% FCF yield, could easily produce a relief gap. The Dell print the same night and a market moving 2-5% a day could swamp HP's own news inside a close-to-open window.
approach_notes: P4/P6 helped most: taking the run-in apart showed the Oct 30 drop was tied to Intel's industry call, which separates what the price holds (the slump) from what it does not (HP's own guide number vs a stale consensus). P7's 65% bar correctly stopped a short on a real but already-crowded thesis.
